title: 27th sitting of the 20th Majlis
presiding: Abdul Raheem Abdulla (Speaker); Ahmed Saleem (Deputy Speaker) chaired part of the bill debate until the 10:31 recess
summary: The sitting opened at 9:01 with announcements of two committee membership changes and a proposal to extend the current session to 26 August 2024, to be voted on later. MPs then questioned the Minister of Construction and Infrastructure about stalled water, sewerage and harbour projects; he said FENAKA contracts are being terminated and re-awarded to MWSC, and that the budget is too small to run every project at once. After four government bills had their first readings, the preliminary debate on the Built Environment Planning and Management Bill began, with MPs speaking for a national planning law and some criticising past land allocation; the debate was still running at the end of this part. MPs finished debating the government's Built Environment Planning and Management Bill. Speakers backed it as a way to stop plots being handed out without a plan, as happened in Hulhumale', and as a way to protect islands from flooding. After a short debate on a bill amending the Decentralization Act, which would link island plans to the new planning law, the Majlis voted to extend the current session to 26 August, accepted both bills, and sent them to a joint committee. Committee meetings were scheduled and the next sitting set for 14 August.

speakers.name: Dr. Abdulla Muthalib
positions: Minister of Construction and Infrastructure: said FENAKA contracts are being terminated and re-awarded to MWSC, with a tender board award expected within weeks.
Said the Thilamale bridge keeps its schedule (Vilingili link Dec 2025, Gulhifalhu Mar 2026, full project Sep 2026).
Said signed 2024 PSIP projects total MVR 36.8 billion against under MVR 5 billion available, so projects must be prioritised.

speakers.name: Ibrahim Nazil
positions: Asked how much money the Dhonfanu project was handed to MWSC for, and how many islands were surveyed or still lack water and sewerage.
Raised a point of order that the budget is drafted by the executive and sent to the Majlis, not made by MPs.
Objected to the minister's remark about the budget and MPs' responsibility.

speakers.name: Maaroof Zakir
positions: Asked why B. Dhonfanu water and sewerage works stalled and when residents will be served, and about stalled Kihaadhoo and Kudarikilu works.
Asked how many water and sewerage projects have stalled nationwide, when the Thilamale bridge will open, and how many islands still lack systems.

speakers.name: Ibrahim Didi
positions: As sponsor, said the bill sets a legal framework for planning and managing the built environment at island, city and regional level.
Said a planning law ties infrastructure projects to long-term plans and makes development sustainable.
As sponsor, thanked members and said the bill would stop planning-free land handouts and help committee-stage improvements.

speakers.name: Mohamed Niushad
positions: Asked how long until services reach Rakeedhoo now that its water and sewerage works are finished.
Asked when a fix would come for erosion at Rakeedhoo where protective boulders have shifted.

speakers.name: Ameen Faisal
positions: Asked whether Sh. Bilehfahi and Noomaraa are among those handed to MWSC, and whether Kanditheemu's silted harbour can be fixed this year.
Said he worked with the council and local government ministry and sent videos and photos; asked if any solution exists this year.

speakers.name: Hassan Zareer
positions: Backed the bill and used Singapore's planned growth as an example; cautioned against offering the country as a second home to foreign investors.
Said plans keep changing every five years, as in Hulhumale'; argued that national planning should cover facilities such as hospitals and airports and be tied to the economy.

speakers.name: Ibrahim Shujau
positions: Asked why the bill came late in the term and said an earlier land use plan for Male' was held up for months.
Argued the bill gives planning legal force and should be refined in committee.

speakers.name: Hassan Mufeed Abdul Gadir
positions: Said no dedicated planning law exists and the 2002 regulation was never gazetted; pointed to Article 10 as setting planning criteria (speech continues in next part).
Supported the amendments as helping resolve development complaints, with economic and environmental assessment; linked the bill to the planning law.

speakers.name: Ahmed Naseer
positions: Argued small islands cannot hold every facility, so nearby islands should share services under a plan.
Said roads and drainage must be designed around flood and storm risks, and earlier houses were built without proper foundations.

speakers.name: Ahmed Didi
positions: Asked when water and sewerage works would start on the land already reclaimed in his constituency.

speakers.name: Hussain Ziyad
positions: Asked when stalled water and sewerage work in Kurinbi would restart, and whether any project has newly started anywhere.

speakers.name: Ahmed Shakir
positions: Asked about the Hithadhoo causeway, water and sewerage at Kunahandhoo, and land reclamation at Maavashu, saying Kunahandhoo's situation is poor.

speakers.name: Abdul Hannan Aboobakuru
positions: Asked when stalled water and sewerage works in Thulhaadhoo, Fulhadhoo and Fehendhoo would restart and finish.

speakers.name: Mohamed Abbas
positions: Asked when Velidhoo's sewerage would restart and when stalled harbour works at Velidhoo and Foddhoo would resume.

speakers.name: Abdul Gafoor Moosa
positions: Said works at Naivaadhoo, Hirimaradhoo and Finey are underway but slow, with staff waiting for fuel; asked if they could be sped up.

speakers.name: Dr. Ahmed Shamheed
positions: Asked whether there is a quick fix, given the housing minister said Gulhifalhu plots cannot be allocated until the bridge project finishes.

speakers.name: Ibrahim Falah
positions: Asked whether projects started by the previous government have funds in the budget, and whether the minister would meet MPs for details of undone work in their constituencies.

speakers.name: Munthazim Ibrahim
positions: Said the lack of planning laws was a neglect by earlier governments and criticised how Hulhumale' plots were allocated; urged thorough debate and amendments.

speakers.name: Mohamed Mamdooh
positions: Said the missing planning law left island development inconsistent and councils and government out of step; hoped the committee consults widely.

speakers.name: Hussain Hameed
positions: Said projects ran without plans, reclaimed land sat idle for years, and atolls empty as services concentrate in Male'; urged more power for councils.

speakers.name: Ahmed Aifan
positions: Backed the bill as needed for long-term planning and criticised how Hulhumale' land was allocated without a plan under the previous government.

speakers.name: Asadhulla Shihab
positions: Thanked the President and the sponsor; said the law should set out how islands and cities are planned and what facilities each must have; called for consequences for officials who ignore it, and for the bill to pass quickly.

speakers.name: Mohamed Musthafa Ibrahim
positions: Said the bill is historic; blamed past land handouts in Hulhumale' without proper plans for crowding and lack of parks; urged a quick committee stage.

speakers.name: Ali Moosa
positions: Said the bill matches international practice; described flooding in Hoarafushi, Uligamu and Thuraakunu caused by missing drainage and sewage planning; asked how well EIAs work in practice.

speakers.name: Abdulla Rifau
positions: Thanked the sponsor; said the lack of a planning law caused past losses and praised the President's housing record, including work in Maafannu.

speakers.name: Mohamed Fazeel
positions: As sponsor, said the amendments let island and city plans be prepared with public input and tie councils' land and investment powers to the physical development plan.

decisions: Chair announced Abdulla Rifau (South Maafannu) joins the Foreign Relations Committee in place of Abdulla Shazeem.
Chair announced Abdulla Shazeem (Central Hulhumale') joins the Environment and Climate Change Committee in place of Mohamed Rasheed (Nolhivaram).
Chair proposed extending the session to Monday 26 August 2024, to be voted on at the day's vote time.
Four government bills (Foreign Investment; Business Registration amendment; Securities amendment; Tourism amendment) were read for the first time.
Session of the Majlis extended to 26 August 2024.
Built Environment Planning and Management Bill accepted for consideration and sent to a joint committee.
Bill amending the Decentralization Act (Law 7/2010) accepted for consideration and sent to the same joint committee.
Next sitting set for 14 August 2024 at 9:00.

votes.what: Extend the current session until 26 August 2024
Accept the Built Environment Planning and Management Bill
Accept the bill to amend the Decentralization Act (Law 7/2010)
